newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Top Kremlin official to oversee Russia WTO bid.
newsitem.headline: Top Kremlin official to oversee Russia WTO bid.

text.p: Russia's First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais has pledged to take personal charge of the country's bid to become a member of the World Trade Organisation (WTO), trade sources said on Wednesday.

They said Chubais had made his promise during a meeting on Tuesday in Washington with World Trade Organisation (WTO) chief Renato Ruggiero in after a meeting of the Group of Seven industrialised countries backed the Russian effort.
"Chubais said he would personally follow the accession process at the WTO and would be handling (in Moscow) at the political level," one source familiar with the discussions with Ruggiero said.

The sources said the young reformer, widely admired in Western capitals although rating low in domestic opinion polls, had told Ruggiero joining the WTO was a "top priority" for Russia and that he wanted to "pick up speed" in the talks.

Trade diplomats said they hoped Chubais, who apparently has the confidence of President Boris Yeltsin, would be able to ensure consistency in the Russian approach to the negotiations, under way for over two years.

Envoys to the 131-member WTO says they have been dismayed by what they see as a lack of understanding among different ministries and government bodies in Moscow at the implications of the membership application.
"The impression is often that the right hand does not know what the left hand is doing," said one trade diplomat.

Earlier this month, the four major trading powers -- the United States, the European Union, Japan and Canada -- appealed to Moscow to implement a freeze, or standstill, on any new trade measures that could toughen current regulations.

But the appeal, made by the four during a meeting of the WTO working party studying the Russian application, was effectively turned down by deputy foreign trade minister Georgy Gabuniya who was leading the Moscow delegation.
Gabuniya said it would be impractical to implement a standstill, given the country's "deep-going economic reform."

China, which has been negotiating entry to the WTO for more than a decade, has agreed to a standstill -- which means that a country cannot toughen its rules to strengthen its negotiating stance while talks are under way.

This week, Russia's central bank said it was tightening regulation of foreign banks in the country to protect the domestic sector -- a move trade diplomats said would be a violation of a standstill if one had been agreed.

WTO countries are currently negotiating for a global agreement on financial services, which is likely to be completed before Russia joins the organisation and to whose terms it would have to subscribe.

The trade sources said Ruggiero told Chubais that the atmosphere for Russian WTO entry was very positive, but stressed the importance for Moscow to come up with a strong package on market access acceptable to present members.
The sources quoted the WTO chief as saying presentation of the market access package, for which no timetable has yet been set, was "the real moment at which negotiations begin."

Although Yeltsin and U.S. President Bill Clinton had agreed at a recent summit in Helsinki that 1998 was the target date for Russia to be admitted, this schedule was "tight, tight," Ruggiero told Chubais, according to the sources.
